thread.title: Tech Today: Amazon Rocks Health Care, Intel Gets a Thumbs Up, Corning Beats

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Amazon Rocks Health Care, Intel Gets a Thumbs Up, Corning Beats
text:
Here are some things going on today in your world of tech :
The Nasdaq Composite index is trending down along with the other major indexes, declining by 73.11 to 7,393.39.
Fiber glows
One bright spot, so to speak, in today’s market are fiber-optic stocks, which had been under pressure lately. Shares of Lumentum ( LITE ) and Finisar ( FNSR ) are going higher after Loop Capital ’s James Kisner late yesterday initiated Lumentum with a Buy rating and Finisar with a Hold rating.
Among other ratings actions, Chris Danely of Citigroup , long a bear on Intel ( INTC ), resumes coverage of the stock this morning with a Buy rating and a $58 price target, applauding the company’s new practice of giving “conservative” forecasts. Intel shares are down a penny at $49.96. This follows Intel’s upbeat Q4 report last week .
Shares of GrubHub ( GRUB ), the online food-ordering startup, are down $3.47, or almost 5%, at $71.95, after the stock was cut to Underweight from Neutral by Barclays ’ Deepak Mathivanan , based on an expectation the company’s outlook for this year could miss expectations.
Amazon, your benefits giant
Shares of Amazon.com ( AMZN ) are down $6.95, or half a percent, at $1,410.73, after the company this morning announced it will work with Berkshire Hathaway ( BRKB ) and JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) to form a nonprofit company to address health care for their employees, with a goal of cutting costs.
Berkshire Chairman Warren Buffett was Quote: d discussing the ballooning costs of health care, as written up by the FT ’s Pan Kwan Yuk and Adam Samson .
One early response this morning comes from Anthony DiClemente of Instinet, who sees several aspects of this as intriguing, including at some point in future providing “ value to Prime customers ,” meaning Amazon’s loyalty membership customers. His colleague, Ross Muken , covering health care, thinks “to the degree they are even remotely successful, this will have massive implications on health-care valuations broadly."
Muken thinks the selloff of some managed-care stocks, such as UnitedHealth Group ( UNH ), which is down about 5%, is a buying opportunity. One health care name spared the knife is Cerner ( CERN ), as apparently there has been a rumor this morning of its partnering with Amazon. But Briefing.com a short while ago stated that it seems that it may be an old rumor from last year. At any rate, Cerner shares are up 88 cents, or 1.3%, at $69.61.
$1,600 new sweet spot for AMZN targets
Speaking of Amazon, whose earnings are on tap for Thursday , after the closing bell, the stock is still getting price target increases as we roll toward that. One comes this morning from Needham & Co .’s Kerry Rice, who raises his target to $1,600 from $1,250, and Guggenheim ’s Robert Drbul, who raises his target to $1,600 from $1,400.
There may others at that number today; I’ve lost track.
Displays, displays everywhere
Shares of glass titan Corning ( GLW ) are down $1.85, or over 5%, at $32.40, despite the company this morning reported Q4 revenue and profit that topped analysts’ expectations, and forecast this year’s sales, $11 billion, above the consensus for $10.7 billion.
In a first pass, Guggenheim’s Robert Cihra , who has a Buy on the stock, notes the core glass business beat his expectations, and that Corning is calling for similar growth in the market for LCD displays as last year, about “single digits.” However, Corning is looking to outgrow the market as its fuels production of displays in China.
Speaking of displays, the Street is still debating what to do with Universal Display ( OLED ), the maker of technology for OLED-based displays, after yesterday’s round of worries about Apple ’s ( AAPL ) iPhone X sales.
Mehdi Hosseini with Susquehanna argues people are wrong in putting blame for iPhone X’s cost on OLED, writing, "In our view, the elevated iPhone BOM cost is mostly driven by other (non-OLED display) components,” such as the price inflation for memory chips . "OLED display, which is a key feature of the iPhone X, is actually within striking distance of reaching cost parity with LCD!” he adds.
Earnings on tap
Reporting this afternoon, after the closing bell, are Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ), Amdocs ( DOX ), Electronic Arts ( EA ), and Juniper Networks ( JNPR ).
